claims.text: Greg Short asserts that the pre-dawn window before other people wake up is the single most guilt-free block for entrepreneurial self-investment: because no family, colleagues, or social obligations are yet active, there are no competing demands that would normally generate guilt or inconvenience when time is spent on personal ambitions.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies to founders and entrepreneurs pursuing ambitious personal or business goals
Requires scheduling personal work before household or social routines begin
claims.mechanism: Before the rest of the household and social circle is awake, there are no competing demands; the absence of observable sacrifice eliminates the guilt that would otherwise accompany prioritizing self-investment over family or social obligations.

claims.text: Greg Short claims that building a consistent habit of waking at 5:00 or 5:30 AM generates a compounding advantage over people who wake later, and characterizes this habit as a major unlock for anyone pursuing ambitious outcomes in their 20s, 30s, or 40s.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Requires regularity (circadian rhythm anchored to early wake time, not occasional early rising)
Applies to individuals in their 20s, 30s, or 40s chasing ambitious personal or professional outcomes

numbers.axis: wake time on the early-morning axis

bounded_by: Greg Short does not address whether the advantage holds without regularity (i.e. occasional early rising is not claimed to produce the same effect)

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that establishing a stable circadian rhythm anchored to an early wake time (5-5:30 AM) is the mechanism by which the morning advantage compounds: irregular early rising does not produce the same effect because the rhythm, once set, removes the daily willpower cost of waking early.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Requires regular adherence until the wake time becomes habitual rather than effortful
claims.mechanism: A stable circadian rhythm anchored to 5-5:30 AM eliminates the daily willpower cost of rising early, making the extra productive hours automatic rather than discretionary.

anchors.value: sporadic early rising, high willpower cost

practices.text: Greg Short advises entrepreneurs to embrace the reality that building a great life requires being selfish with time, and to treat early morning hours as the designated window for that selfishness.
Target waking at 5:00 or 5:30 AM daily and build it into a stable circadian rhythm to capture the compounding advantage of uninterrupted early-morning work time.
